A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAMPO and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E. Matching content across pagination and citation changes supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SAMPO results for video prediction, VP2 planning, Meta-World reinforcement learning, ablations, and zero-shot generation.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds configuration-specific VP2 success results in Table 5.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same hybrid autoregression, asymmetric tokenizer, trajectory-aware motion prompts, training objectives, and inference procedures.

E1.justification: Open X-Embodiment pretraining and the BAIR, RoboNet, 1X, VP2, Meta-World, and zero-shot evaluation coverage remain unchanged. The added VP2 scale comparisons concern an existing task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–5, the reinforcement-learning comparison, and appendix visualizations. Table 5 retains the same AR138M baseline, citing iVideoGPT under its updated reference number.

E3.justification: Table 5 extends the spatial-scale comparison to VP2 average success alongside the existing BAIR prediction and timing measurements. This adds control evaluation for the retained scale configurations; existing splits, budgets, and benchmark procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 5 adds evidence about how spatial-scale choices affect control success, extending the existing fidelity–speed sensitivity analysis. Component ablations, model-size analyses, zero-shot examples, and appendix case studies are otherwise unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains task-level means and standard deviations across three seeds, and Figure 5 retains 95% confidence intervals from five seeds. The added Table 5 column contains point estimates without new seed or uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds VP2 success rates of 72.2, 71.3, and 70.6 for scales [1,2,4,8], [1,2,4,8,10], and [1,2,3,4,5,6], respectively, alongside AR's 70.1. The 72.2 SAMPO and 70.1 baseline averages already appeared in Table 3; the configuration-specific comparison is new. Previously reported prediction scores, timings, RL curves, and qualitative results are retained.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation, autoregressive factorizations, tokenizer and trajectory definitions, and loss and scaling equations (1–8) are unchanged. No theoretical results or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about SAMPO's architecture, motion prompting, prediction and control performance, 4.4-fold inference speedup, generalization, and scaling.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and interpretations remain unchanged, as do the single-frame prompting limitations in Appendix D and long-horizon error accumulation discussed in Section 5. The added VP2 column receives no new substantive interpretation.

D1.justification: Section 3.5 and Appendices A–B retain the same implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware and training costs, preprocessing algorithm, and code/data access information. The added scores do not introduce a new implementation recipe.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Embodiedreamer, DriveDreamer4D, ReconDreamer++, FlowRAM, and PDFactor. The two Ha–Schmidhuber 2018 entries in v1 are reduced to the retained World models entry. Research-positioning prose otherwise remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 adds a funding Acknowledgement section after the conclusion. The main narrative and appendix organization remain substantially unchanged, with localized caption, citation, and text-reflow edits.

P2.justification: Table 5 gains an average-success column and expands from a small table beside wrapped prose to a full-width table above Figure 6. This causes local reflow; existing figure content and appendix displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The expanded Table 5 provides useful evidence for choosing spatial scales: the configuration with the best BAIR FVD reports lower VP2 success than the four-scale configuration. Its larger presentation also improves readability. These are limited gains because the added comparison receives no configuration-specific uncertainty or explanatory discussion, while the core method and existing evidence remain unchanged.
